briefHtml:
NAV S$10,251,546 — reported -0.21% (approx +0.06% real; Oct 15 base restated down to 10,245,143). Biggest verified mover: Seatrium -4.6% to S$1.85, the STI's worst performer Thursday; Xiaomi rose again +2.65% to HK$27.08 (+8.1% in two days) while Korea's memory crash triggered a KOSPI circuit breaker. One thing: PPI came in double-hot (+1.3% m/m, 6.3% y/y) and retail sales doubled estimates — yet Treasury yields FELL a second day (10y -10bp to ~5.09%, settling ~5.06%), October hike odds round-tripped to ~30%, and Treasury executed its $6bn buyback. BTIG calls it a bond-market 'news failure': the 5.20% duration gate for the Defense sleeve is now cracked open. TSMC's blowout Q4 guide ($52.3-54.3bn) confirms the AI-hardware cycle even as memory crashes.

State (fresh snapshot 07:40 SGT)

  • NAV S$10,251,546; reported -0.211%; listed sleeve -1.195% (contaminated by the stale SMIC flag). Oct 15 restated to 10,245,143. NAV level authoritative.
  • FX: USD/SGD 1.2820 (dollar eased post-PPI), CNY/SGD 0.191879 (USDCNY ~6.681), HKD/SGD 0.163377, MYR/SGD 0.314216.
  • priceErrors: L46.SI Yahoo 404 — 26th consecutive session.

Flag integrity — both partly stale

  • SMIC -8.2% in a day (0.9% NW): exaggerated — actual Thursday close HK$52.15, -3.96%. The real story is cumulative: -14.4% from Oct 7's 60.90. Thursday broke the 53.75 gate — semis re-entry NOT armed.
  • Silver -4.7% / line equity -7.0%: stale by one session — that was Wednesday's crash (settle $55.64, -5.98%). Thursday silver REBOUNDED +2.4% to ~$56.9-57; gold +1.5%.

Position moves (Thu Oct 15)

  • SGX: STI 5,403.50 -0.37% (intraday lowest since Jul 8). DBS 73.75 -0.79%. Seatrium -4.6% to 1.85, worst STI performer; YZJ -4.1% intraday.
  • HK: HSI 24,062.72 -1.03%. Xiaomi 27.08 +2.65%; Tencent ~417.9 -1.3%; SMIC 52.15 -3.96%. Lenovo -14.5%. Transsion's HK debut cited 'rising memory costs' — counter-nuance to the BOM-relief thesis.
  • Korea/Japan crash: KOSPI -7.57%, circuit breaker (first since Jul 29); Samsung -9.5%, SK Hynix -11.1%; Nikkei -4.9%.
  • US: Dow +1.1% (+~550 pts) / SPX +0.3% (7,745) / Nasdaq +0.1% / RUT +1.4% — rotation out of mega-cap tech; equal-weight +1%. VIX 16.46 -2.4% (faded from 18.01). 10y ~5.09% (-10bp, settled ~5.06%); DXY 102.00 -0.5%.
  • Metals rebounded: gold +1.5% (~$4,150-4,170), silver +2.4% (~$56.9-57); SILJ ~27.08 +1.2%. Oil: WTI settled +2.6% at $97.97 after an EIA -8.557M bbl draw; Brent $105.92.
  • TSMC Q3 blowout: revenue $46.72bn (+41.2% y/y), GM 66.4%, EPS $4.60 beat; Q4 guided $52.3-54.3bn (+14% q/q); capex $60-64bn.

Insider trades (7d)

  • Wing Tai (W05.SI): NEW Oct 13 'Change in Interest of Director' adds to Oct 12 (+ treasury-share transfer notice), Oct 9 (same pairing) and Oct 6 (+ share-award grant) — four director-interest filings in eight days atop a six-filing late-Sep cluster; Cheng concert group ~63%. Counts not disclosed; treasury-transfer pairings read as Buy-equivalents.
  • None found for other held SGX names or Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi on HKEX in the window. US holdings are ETFs — no insider filings exist.

Congress trades (filed Oct 13-14; no new filings Oct 15-16 as of 07:45 SGT)

  • PA-9 (R): SOLD NVDA $1-15K (trade 8/31).
  • OK-1 (R): rotation out of equities into Oklahoma munis — sold NEE, ROK, SBUX, Virtus AI ETF, LMT x4, MRSH x2, CVX, DVN x2, EMR, HD, LIN, LOW, CB.
  • CA-31 (D): ~80-line reshuffle; bought TSM, NXPI x2, ON Semi; sold AVGO, MCHP, MTSI x2, WDC, SMTC.
  • MI-9 (R): bought OLN, RIG, CACI, CAT, MSFT, Novagold (NG); SOLD STX $15-50K on 9/30 — days before the memory crash.
  • WA-2 (D): sold FDX, HD; bought WSM. Pattern: members sold memory pre-crash, rotated into Asia semis, munis and a gold miner.

Trump / policy watch (24-48h)

  • PPI double-hot, bonds don't care: PPI +1.3% m/m / 6.3% y/y (core 5.0% vs 4.4% exp); retail sales +0.8% (gasoline-led). Yet 10y -10bp, October hike odds back to ~30% from ~50%, Treasury bought back $6bn of 20-30y ($40.84bn offered). September PCE expectations revised UP. Warsh speaks at the IMF today.
  • Hormuz — a Singapore flag sinks: CENTCOM says the Singapore-flagged M/V GFS Pride sank after an IRGC projectile (not a mine); Iran's Army Commander: Hormuz 'closed until rights respected'; Hezbollah told to prepare for war; Tehran weighs NPT withdrawal; 120 vessels blacklisted; fresh US Iran sanctions; Netanyahu-Rubio call.
  • Oil stockpile politics: EIA crude -8.557M bbls; US wants +100M bbls added to the IEA emergency release; IEA completing 100M + seeking 20M diesel ASAP; SPR unchanged at 44-yr low.
  • Trade walls: EU assessing more quota sectors on Chinese imports + a tool that could block China from the single market; UK may align with EU EV tariffs; India-US phase one finalised; China bought 10-13 US soybean cargoes.
  • AI demand confirmed at source: TSMC Q4 guide +14% q/q on 2nm ramp; counterpoint — CoreWeave's 15% bond yield (financing-chain stress); Google quantum breakthrough; Tesla energy VP exits on AI pivot.
  • Today: Singapore Sep non-oil exports, Korea unemployment, US import/export prices; Warsh (IMF), Bailey, Macklem speak. Next: Meta/Tesla Oct 21, FOMC Oct 27-28, GDP Oct 29.

Risk

  • Watcher flags: SMIC exaggerated (actual -3.96%); silver flag stale (rebounded +2.4%).
  • Silver line recovering but thin: ~S$129.5k collateral vs S$56,240 loan; equity ~S$73.3k; ratio ~1.77x (vs 1.80x at Wednesday's settle, 1.70x pre-CPI). A renewed -4% silver day still cuts ~7% of equity.
  • 'News failure' cuts both ways: yield relief is partly haven flow from the memory rout — a TSMC-led tech bounce could reverse it; FOMC Oct 27-28 looms (Oct ~30%, Dec near-certain).
  • Korea contagion: circuit breakers + Samsung/SK Hynix -9~-11% = forced deleveraging risk into HK semis (SMIC -14% from Oct 7).
  • War escalation: Singapore-flagged vessel sunk; Hormuz 'closed'; emergency-release politics signal supply-panic management — energy volatility bid.
  • Seatrium -4.6% (small, ~S$37k); FX ~35% non-SGD with USD/SGD easing to 1.2820; DBS -0.79%; L46.SI feed down 26th session.

Alpha (signals, not advice; ~62% of liquid book idle cash)

  • Defense sleeve (target 15%) — duration gate CRACKED OPEN: 10y ~5.09%/5.06%, decisively below the 5.20% threshold, after TWO hot inflation prints. Signal: 10y holding sub-5.10% through Warsh's IMF speech and the weekend = first duration-entry trigger (TIPS/long duration); size small — the bid is partly haven flow.
  • Xiaomi 1810.HK — divergence keeps paying: +2.65% Thursday (+8.1% in two days) while KOSPI circuit-broke and Lenovo -14.5%; TSMC's guide confirms the device cycle. Watch Transsion's 'rising memory costs' counter-signal. Signal: hold/build above ~HK$26.4.
  • Asia semis (SMIC/TSM) — rout is memory-specific: TSMC blowout vs KOSPI crash = CXMT/DRAM, not foundry demand. SMIC broke the gate (52.15 under 53.75) — entry NOT armed. New signal: SMIC reclaiming ~HK$54 + TSM ADR green Friday = entry; below 51.05 = stay out. Silver reload stays on watch: $55-56 held, line ~1.77x — a second stabilizing session opens the scale-in window.

trumpWatch.title: PPI double-hot, bonds shrug: yields fall again, October odds back to ~30%, $6bn buyback executed
trumpWatch.detail: September PPI +1.3% m/m and 6.3% y/y (core +0.7% m/m, 5.0% y/y vs 4.4% exp) — hotter than CPI; retail sales +0.8% m/m vs +0.3% exp (gasoline-station led; control group missed); claims 199K; NY Empire 25.5 beat, Philly Fed 20.9 missed. Yet the 10y fell ~10bp to ~5.09% (settled ~5.06%), October hike odds fell back to ~30% from ~50%, and Treasury's liquidity buyback accepted $6bn of $40.84bn offered in 20-30y. BTIG: bond-market 'news failure' — yields may have peaked. September PCE expectations revised up; Fed Chair Warsh speaks at the IMF Friday.

trumpWatch.title: Hormuz: Singapore-flagged M/V GFS Pride sank after IRGC projectile, says CENTCOM
trumpWatch.detail: CENTCOM rejected the IRGC's claim to control the strait and said the Singapore-flagged container ship was hit by an IRGC projectile (not a mine) and sank while under tow; it denied Iranian claims of hundreds of US deaths in Jordan. Iran's Army Commander: Hormuz 'will remain closed until the rights of the Iranian people are respected'. Iran warned Hezbollah to prepare for war (Jerusalem Post); Tehran considering NPT withdrawal (Tasnim); 120 vessels blacklisted; two more tankers reported on fire east of the strait; US issued fresh Iran-related sanctions; Netanyahu told Rubio military action is 'a realistic scenario' if Tehran does not come to its senses.

trumpWatch.title: Oil: huge EIA draw, US pushes IEA for +100M bbls more emergency release
trumpWatch.detail: EIA crude stocks fell 8.557M bbls (exp -0.3M) in the week to Oct 9; SPR unchanged at 283M bbls (44-yr low). US told IEA members it is unhappy with the planned emergency release and suggested supplementing it with a further 100M bbls; IEA agreed to complete the outstanding 100M release and is seeking a 20M-bbl diesel release ASAP. WTI settled +$2.88 at $97.97; Brent -$0.14 at $105.92.

trumpWatch.title: Trade walls: EU weighs quotas and a tool that could block China from the single market
trumpWatch.detail: EU assessing additional sectors for potential trade quotas on Chinese imports and planning a trade instrument that could block China from the single market; UK could align with EU tariffs on Chinese EVs (Politico); France/Germany would include the UK in 'Made in Europe' if it aligns on China tariffs (FT); India-US phase-one deal finalised and in legal drafting; China's state trader bought 10-13 US soybean cargoes for Dec-Mar shipment.

trumpWatch.title: TSMC blowout confirms AI demand: Q4 guided +14% q/q; capex $60-64bn
trumpWatch.detail: Q3 revenue $46.72bn (+41.2% y/y, above guidance top), gross margin 66.4% (in range), net income NT$763.06bn (+68.7%), EPS $4.60 vs $4.45 exp; Q4 revenue guided $52.3-54.3bn (+14% q/q) on leading-edge demand and the 2nm ramp; 7nm-and-below = 79% of wafer revenue; 2026 capex $60-64bn. Counterpoints: CoreWeave's 15% bond yield (AI financing-chain stress); Google published a quantum-computing breakthrough; Tesla's energy/charging VP departed as Tesla pivots to AI (WSJ).

trumpWatch.title: Regionals: KOSPI circuit breaker (-7.57%); Friday brings Singapore exports and Warsh at the IMF
trumpWatch.detail: KOSPI -7.57% with the first market-wide halt since Jul 29 (Samsung -9.5%, SK Hynix -11.1%); Nikkei -4.9%; Japan MoF monitoring markets closely; PBoC reiterates moderately loose policy. Friday: Singapore September non-oil exports, South Korea unemployment, US import/export prices; speakers: Fed Chair Warsh (IMF), BoE Bailey, BoC Macklem. Next week: Meta/Tesla earnings Oct 21; FOMC Oct 27-28; US GDP Oct 29.

opportunities.thesis: Duration gate cracked open: the 10y closed ~5.09% / settled ~5.06%, decisively below the 5.20% threshold — and it happened after TWO hot inflation prints (CPI Wednesday, PPI Thursday). BTIG 'news failure' says yields may have peaked; October hike odds back to ~30%; Treasury executed a $6bn buyback of 20-30y. With ~62% of the liquid book idle cash, the Defense sleeve is the most under-deployed target.
opportunities.signal: 10y holding sub-5.10% through Warsh's IMF speech Friday and into the weekend = first duration-entry trigger (TIPS/long duration). Size small: part of the bid is haven flow from the memory rout, which could unwind on TSMC-led tech relief.

opportunities.thesis: The divergence keeps paying: +2.65% Thursday to HK$27.08 (+8.1% in two days) while KOSPI circuit-broke (-7.57%), Samsung/SK Hynix fell 9-11%, and Lenovo -14.5%. TSMC's +14% q/q Q4 guide confirms the hardware/device cycle. Counter-signal to watch: Transsion's HK debut cited 'rising memory costs and margin pressures' — OEM contract relief lags the DRAM spot crash.
opportunities.signal: Hold/build above ~HK$26.4 (Wednesday's close). A close back below 26.4 ends the leg; above it, the BOM-relief + AI-device thesis compounds.

SMIC broke Thursday's gate (closed 52.15 under 53.75) so entry is NOT armed, but the washout is approaching the 49.32 52-week low with utilization at 93.7%.
opportunities.signal: SMIC reclaiming ~HK$54 + TSM ADR green on Friday's TSMC reaction = semis-leg entry; SMIC below 51.05 (Thursday low) = stay out. Silver reload (Real Assets 20%) stays on watch: $55-56 held Thursday, line ~1.77x — a second stabilizing session opens the scale-in window.
